items.title: Trump's White House media ban faces long odds in court
items.summary: US President Donald Trump's move to ban several news outlets from the White House over his dislike of their coverage likely runs afoul of US legal prohibitions against viewpoint discrimination by the government, four legal experts told Reuters. Trump said on Saturday that he might ban other outlets as well. The White House said in a statement that the news outlets were completely capable of reporting from outside the White House.

items.title: Police announce three‑stage road closures for Kuching Marathon from Sept 26 to 27
items.summary: These include the Jalan Pearl-Jalan Wawasan traffic lights towards Padang Merdeka, Lebuh Wayang-Jalan Wawasan, Jalan McDougall-Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg, and Susur Jalan Haji Taha. Also affected are the Jalan Ajibah Abol traffic lights, Jalan Muhibbah-Jalan Kulas junction, Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob-Jalan Merdeka junction, Jalan Kampung Lintang-Jalan Astana traffic lights, Mahkamah roundabout, Sesco roundabout, and Samariang roundabout. The closures will also cover the Jalan Sultan Tengah traffic lights near the fire station and Sego, Yayasan roundabout, Kesuma Resort roundabout, Stadium roundabout, Gersik roundabout, Merrican Salleh-Jalan Kwong Lee Bank traffic lights, Tanah Putih Clinic traffic lights, Jalan Sekama-Pending traffic lights, Sri Aman roundabout, and Jalan Gamelan-Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob junction.

items.title: Man dies in suspected electrocution in Lahad Datu
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Sept 23 — A man in his 30s died after he was believed to have been electrocuted at Kampung Puyut here today. The man, who had yet to be identified, was believed to have no identification document and was not recognised by local villagers, said Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid. He said the department received a distress call at 12.47pm and deployed 12 personnel to the scene, where the man was found electrocuted and was later confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel.

items.title: Court: Boy's acquittal in Bandar Utama murder must not diminish victim's life, family's grief
items.summary: In concluding the grounds of judgment, judge Adlin Abdul Majid said the court's finding of unsoundness of mind and the boy's acquittal of the murder charge did not mean the fatal attack had not occurred or that no one was responsible. She said the finding was not intended, and should not be understood, to diminish the victim's life or cause anyone to forget her. Adlin said that the victim's family continued to bear profound grief, adding that a diagnosis could not diminish their loss.

items.title: Bring umbrellas: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in KL and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states affected are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kedah, the areas expected to be affected are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak. The same warning has been issued for Kelantan, covering Jeli and Kuala Krai; Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu); and Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan).

items.title: Diving industry backs tighter rules, protection for Sabah guides
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah diving industry players have welcomed the new Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (MOTAC) licensing requirements for dive guides. Sabah Dive Squad Club president Sim Fui said regulation was important to raise accountability and safety standards. However, he said it should also protect the livelihoods of Sabah's local dive guides and instructors.

items.title: Two suffer burns in Bayan Baru restaurant fire
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Two people suffered first-degree burns after a fire broke out in the kitchen of a restaurant in Tingkat Mahsuri, Bayan Baru. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the fire involved the kitchen area, measuring about 10ft by 15ft (3m by 4.6m), with overall damage estimated at 20 per cent. "The two victims suffered first-degree burns and went to a nearby clinic for treatment," he said.

items.title: Anwar: Negeri Sembilan MB and executive council’s bid to remove ruler was ‘rude and uncivilised’
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim criticised the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council for attempting to remove Yang di‑Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, calling the move rude and uncivilised. He said no state‑level authority has the mandate to question or alter the position of the Ruler, according to Berita Harian . Anwar said the crisis involving state administration and customary authority in Negeri Sembilan had become increasingly complex.

items.title: Rehda seeks stamp duty relief, targted HOC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia for the 2027 Budget. The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units. Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.

items.title: Kuala Nerang bomb discovery: Unexploded 60mm mortar round found near Sungai Padang Terap
items.summary: KUALA NERANG: A landscaping worker and two colleagues found a mortar round while carrying out maintenance work near Sungai Padang Terap here at 10.30am today. Padang Terap district police chief Superintendent Mohd Anuar Junoh said police were alerted to the discovery and dispatched a team to the location near Kuala Nerang town for further investigation. "Members of the Kedah Contingent Police Headquarters Bomb Disposal Unit (UPB) who inspected the object found it to be a 60mm 'UXO Mortar' round," he said when contacted.

items.title: Gunmen kill 11 in South African township
items.summary: DURBAN: Gunmen stormed a homestead in a township in South Africa's eastern port city of Durban, killing 11 people, the head of the provincial government and police said on Wednesday. South Africa is awash with legal and illegal firearms, and shootings are common, often fuelled by gang rivalry and competition between informal businesses. Three other people survived the attack in the township of KwaMakhutha south of Durban, police said.

items.title: Conference of Rulers asked to scrutinise Negri Ruler's removal, Undang Luak dismissals
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Conference of Rulers has been asked to scrutinise and advise on the issue surrounding the removal of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from the throne, as well as the dismissal of Undang Luak. The Negri Sembilan Malay Customary Lawyers' Bar (Secretariat), in a joint statement, said the issue should not be confined to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, but should also take into account the dismissal of the Undang Luak. "The dismissal of the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong and other Undang Luak also touches on the position of the Rulers under the interpretation of the UUTKNS 1959, as the Undang Luak also hold such status within the state's constitutional framework.

items.title: Malaysian arrested over alleged S$500,000 scam in Singapore
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police handed over a Malaysian man to their Singapore counterparts yesterday after he allegedly masterminded a cross-border scam syndicate. The 27-year-old suspect allegedly masterminded a syndicate involved in government official impersonation scams and money laundering operations in Singapore. He is said to have used Malaysian runners to collect cash and gold from victims in Singapore.

items.title: Chinese tourist drowns while snorkelling in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A Chinese tourist in her 30s drowned while snorkelling off Pulau Mengalum here today. Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said police received a report on the incident at about 1.30pm. Shahrudin said police who inspected the scene found no criminal element and had recorded statements from witnesses to assist investigations.

items.title: 18-year-old remanded over alleged sexual assault of 16-year-old girl
items.summary: KANGAR: Police have detained an 18-year-old unemployed man after he was alleged to have sexually assaulted a 16-year-old girl in Taman Bukit Kubu, Kuala Perlis, last month. Kangar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the suspect was detained after the girl lodged a report at the Kuala Perlis police station yesterday. He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred around 2am on Aug 29, when the girl was with the suspect at a friend's house.

items.title: North Korea appears to have tested upgraded hypersonic weapon: Analysts
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea appears to have tested a hypersonic weapon that could evade missile defences and prove hard to track and intercept, analysts told AFP Wednesday. North Korea did not identify the weapon, saying only that its missile bureau had "successfully tested a new type of weapon" in a demonstration of "ultra-modern defence technology." Analysts said the weapon appeared to be an upgraded version of North Korea's Hwasongpho-11Ma-1 hypersonic short-range ballistic missile.

items.title: 'No suspension notice received' — Negri state legal adviser reports to work
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal reported for work as usual today despite the state government announcing her immediate suspension yesterday. Muzalmah said she was complying with the directive from Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to remain and serve in Negri Sembilan. Last night, the A-GC said the Negri Sembilan state executive council has no legal authority to suspend the state secretary and state legal adviser.

items.title: Anwar asks Loke to review decision to quit Cabinet after Najib’s conditional pardon
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Transport Minister Anthony Loke to rethink his plan to step down from the Cabinet following the Pardons Board’s decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon. In a New Straits Times report, Anwar said DAP should not give in to political pressure from groups seeking instability in the unity government. “Some people ask, why Anthony Loke?

items.title: Sepang Aircraft lands 12-year Cebu Pacific MRO contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sepang Aircraft Engineering Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Airbus, has secured a 12-year aircraft maintenance contract from Philippine carrier Cebu Pacific covering seven A320 aircraft. The agreement expands an existing relationship between Sepang Aircraft and Cebu Pacific. Sepang Aircraft has also occasionally deployed engineers to Manila to support Cebu Pacific's aircraft maintenance requirements.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for KL, 10 states
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states were Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kedah, the warning covers Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, it affects Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak. The warning also covers Jeli and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; and Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan in Pahang.

items.title: Upstream players seek closer Petronas ties amid uncertainties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's upstream oil and gas industry is seeking closer engagement with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) to strengthen the sector's operating environment amid growing geopolitical and supply-chain uncertainties. The Petroleum Production Sharing Contractors (PPSC) Committee under the Malaysian International Chamber of Commerce & Industry (Micci) recently held its annual engagement with Petronas through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM). The engagement brought together upstream production sharing contractors and industry representatives to discuss key issues affecting the sector.

items.title: Anwar says PH open to talks with any party ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: HANGZHOU: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to talks with any party ahead of the Melaka state election, including Bersatu. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the coalition's openness was for the good of the country's political landscape. He said arrogance and a refusal to negotiate should be avoided in politics when a party expressed willingness to hold talks.

items.title: Seat allocation remains key issue ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Barisan Nasional wanted to retain the 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election, leaving limited room for potential partners. He said any agreement would also depend on whether the parties could convince their grassroots machinery to accept the arrangement and campaign together. He said an understanding between PH and Bersatu could also emerge, while BN, PH and PN could contest separately if negotiations failed.

items.title: In Bangladesh, Pakistan's Jinnah photo stirs anger
items.summary: PAKISTAN founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah died nearly eight decades ago, but his photograph has become the centrepiece of a fresh battle over history at Bangladesh's top university. Abu Tayyab Habildar, the university student who ripped the photograph, called Jinnah a "villain." "In Bangladesh, Jinnah was never celebrated," said political analyst Altaf Parvez.

items.title: Teen assaulted mother days before fatal Bandar Utama school stabbing — psychiatric report
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Just 13 days before a 15-year-old boy fatally stabbed his 16-year-old schoolmate at a Bandar Utama school last year, he assaulted his mother when she tried to inspect his bag. The incident was revealed in a psychiatric report by Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta director and forensic consultant psychiatrist Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony. The boy had been seeing a school counsellor following repeated complaints that he was coming late to school, sleeping in class and having long hair.

items.title: Structural checks at Cheras apartment will take several days following landslide, says Selangor exco
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents evacuated from Block D of the Damai Perdana Apartments in Cheras may have to remain out of their homes for several days while authorities determine whether the building is structurally safe. Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Zone 6 councillor Tan Kah Hoe said multiple technical agencies were conducting assessments of the affected block, according to New Straits Times . Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras were ordered to evacuate their homes last night after a landslide occurred near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak.

items.title: Anwar slams MB, state exco move to remove Negri Sembilan Ruler
items.summary: HANGZHOU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the move by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and the state executive councilors to remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from the throne as disrespectful and uncivilised. "The menteri besar and state exco made the decision. "The Undang cannot simply make a decision.

items.title: KLIA still Asia Pacific's most connected megahub, retains 4th spot globally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has retained its position as Asia Pacific's most connected megahub and the world's fourth most connected international airport, according to OAG's 2026 Megahubs Index. OAG said KLIA's capacity grew 6.9 per cent, supported by an expanding airline network that has added seven new scheduled carriers and nine new routes so far this year. The new links include Riyadh, Algeria and Jinan, while Malaysia Airlines has strengthened connectivity with Japan through its new direct Fukuoka-Kuala Lumpur service.

items.title: Sabah man bites ex-girlfriend and threatens to kill her, gets RM5,800 fine
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A 35-year-old man was fined RM5,800 after pleading guilty to hurting his ex-girlfriend and threatening to kill her. Mohd Aideed Husein pleaded guilty before two Magistrates, Dzul Elmy Yunus and Marilyn Kelvin, to separate charges over the incident involving the 30-year-old woman on Sept 15. Before Dzul Elmy, he was fined RM1,800, in default six months’ jail, under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to the woman outside a shop at Lorong Suria Inanam 1.

items.title: Foul smell, black water raise concerns over Sungai Sengkuang
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A foul smell from Sungai Sengkuang, an offshoot of Sungai Tebrau located just 5km from the country's entry point, has raised concerns among residents and motorists using the Eastern Dispersal Link (EDL). Residents in nearby areas, including Taman Sri Stulang, Kampung Tengah and Taman Iskandar, said the stench persisted regardless of the tide, while the river water had also turned black. PPR Sri Stulang resident Ain Mohd Sulaiman, 30, said the worsening stench had affected residents' daily lives, with the smell entering their homes.

items.title: Myanmar post-coup leader says 'lenient' on Suu Kyi: Report
items.summary: YANGON: Myanmar's coup leader turned civilian president Min Aung Hlaing said in an interview published Wednesday he has been "extremely lenient" on Aung San Suu Kyi, who he ousted and jailed in 2021. "I have been extremely lenient toward her," Min Aung Hlaing said, according to an interview with US magazine Time. Min Aung Hlaing retired as military chief to become civilian president in April, following elections derided by rights groups as a charade.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines extends Airbus support for A330 fleet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has extended its flight hour services (FHS) contract with Airbus for its A330ceo fleet, reinforcing a maintenance partnership that has been in place since 2017. Malaysia Airlines will also have access to Airbus' engineering expertise and regional FHS representatives to support its day-to-day maintenance operations. Airbus Asia Pacific president Anand Stanley said the extension reflected Malaysia Airlines' confidence in the FHS programme.

items.title: Philippine Senate lowers threshold to oust VP Duterte
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippine Senate approved on Wednesday a lower threshold of votes needed to find Vice President Sara Duterte guilty at her impeachment trial, potentially making it easier to execute her ouster. Senators voted 13-1, with six Duterte allies abstaining, that the constitutionally required two-thirds guilty verdict by "all members of the Senate" refers only to those "capable of participating." Duterte's lawyers can still appeal the lower threshold at the Supreme Court.

items.title: PM takes high-speed train to Hangzhou after Shanghai event
items.summary: SHANGHAI: After delivering his keynote address at the Plenary Session of the WorldSkills Shanghai, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Malaysian delegation hurried to Hangzhou. However, the prime minister opted to travel to Hangzhou, about 170km from Shanghai, by high-speed train. Also on the journey were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Loke and Malaysia's Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.

items.title: Expedite court proceedings to settle Negeri Sembilan royal dispute, says ex-minister Syed Hamid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Court proceedings related to the Negeri Sembilan royal institution dispute should be expedited to provide a definitive resolution to the legal questions involved, former law minister Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar said. He said the dispute, which involves the adat (customary practices), state law and the Federal Constitution, should be resolved through the legal process rather than public debate or sentiment. Syed Hamid also urged all parties to refrain from making conflicting public statements, saying these could heighten public anxiety and make it more difficult to reach a reasonable and rational resolution.

items.title: 81pct of developers report higher business costs in 1H 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia's market survey showed that 81 per cent of respondents reported higher costs of doing business in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), up from 74 per cent in the second half of 2025 (2H 2025). The survey, which involved 181 respondents, indicated that among those reporting higher costs, 35 per cent recorded an increase of between three and six per cent. Zaini said the increase was partly driven by higher prices for diesel-related products, including bitumen, following the Middle East conflict, which particularly affected road, earthworks and infrastructure projects.

items.title: Cambodia no 'safe haven' for cyberscams, PM says
items.summary: PHNOM PENH: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet told an anti-fraud summit Wednesday that his country would never be a "safe haven" for cyberscams, as international partners touted law enforcement successes but warned more must be done. "Cambodia will never be a safe haven for online scams," Hun Manet told a conference against online scams organised by his government in the capital Phnom Penh. He said Cambodian authorities had "completely dismantled all light-scale scam compounds" in a high-profile crackdown launched last year.

items.title: Medini gains another GBS tenant as Teleperformance expands Malaysian footprint
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Investment Bhd (IIB) says Teleperformance has opened a new operation at Menara IIB in Medini, Johor, strengthening the area's position as a regional global business services (GBS) hub. IIB president and chief executive officer Datuk Idzham Mohd Hashim said Teleperformance's presence adds to Medini's growing business ecosystem and strengthens its proposition as a base for regional operations. IIB said 47 GBS companies have established operations in Medini since 2013, supporting about 7,200 jobs.

items.title: TVET graduates may have jobs, but are they the right jobs? MEF asks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a broader assessment of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduate employability to better reflect their skills, career progression and contribution to the workforce. MEF senior adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the federation supported Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir’s call for the employability of Polytechnic and Community College (PolyCC) graduates to be assessed beyond headline employment percentages. He said the 2025 employability rates of 98.5 per cent for polytechnic graduates and 98.8 per cent for community college graduates were encouraging, but the quality and relevance of employment should also be considered in evaluating TVET outcomes.

items.title: Kota Bharu trader’s no-show lands him an arrest warrant over 42 cooking oil charges
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — The Sessions Court here today issued an arrest warrant for the owner of a subsidised cooking oil business after he failed to appear before the court to face charges involving the management of records and documents for the controlled item. Judge Nik Habri Muhamad issued the arrest warrant for Pui Tiong Lam, 61, for failing to appear in court for today’s prosecution proceedings without a valid reason. The court set Nov 5 for mention.

items.title: AG says Negeri Sembilan state secretary and legal adviser remain in office, must continue duties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Negeri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal must continue carrying out their duties because their suspension by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is invalid. Dusuki said, “The duties of Mohd Zafir as Negeri Sembilan state secretary and Muzalmah as state legal adviser must continue as usual, and they must also remain in Negeri Sembilan.” Dusuki said the situation in Negeri Sembilan mirrors the 2009 Perak crisis, when the state secretary and state legal adviser were also suspended.

items.title: Kelantan telecoms at risk of major outages as cable vandalism and theft soar, says says regional MCMC official
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — Vandalism and theft of telecommunications infrastructure in Kelantan have reached an alarming level and could disrupt communication coverage and the livelihoods of people if critical infrastructure is affected. Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Eastern Region Office senior director Mohd Fairus Muhamad said these incidents have also impacted the telecommunications industry, which bears millions of ringgit in losses for repair and restoration work. He said MCMC, together with enforcement authorities and industry players, is tightening coordination, including proposing a Telecommunications Infrastructure Vandalism Prevention Sub-Committee involving MCMC, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities, the Land and District Office and industry players.

items.title: Psychosis impaired teen’s understanding he was taking a life in Bandar Utama school murder, court says, rejecting months‑long planning claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The Shah Alam High Court rejected claims that the 16-year-old schoolgirl’s murder in Bandar Utama last year was planned for months, finding that the accused’s psychotic illness impaired his understanding of the act and that the alleged “plan” stemmed from his delusions. In her full written grounds, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said she could not accept that merely knowing he was pushing a knife into the deceased’s abdomen and that it would cause her to bleed was sufficient to establish that the accused understood the nature of the act. She added that an accused who has knowledge of the mechanics but not of the reality of what he is doing cannot be said to know the nature of the act.

items.title: Budget 2027 wishlist: Rehda wants wider housing loan access, special campaign for unsold units
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) Malaysia for Budget 2027. The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units. Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.

items.title: Who was he? A month on, mystery deepens over man found dead in KLIA aircraft landing gear
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 23 — The identity of a man whose body was found in an aircraft’s landing gear compartment at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 on Aug 27 remains unknown and the remains have yet to be claimed. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police had yet to receive any information that could establish the man’s identity. Asked how the man came to be inside the aircraft, Shazeli said the circumstances remained a mystery and were still under investigation.

items.title: Former Kelantan Kafa teacher gets RM2,000 fine for kicking Year Five pupil in face during class
items.summary: KUALA KRAI, Sept 23 — A former Religious and Fardu Ain Class (Kafa) teacher was fined RM2,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today for kicking a Year Five pupil in the face, causing injuries to his gums. Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid imposed the maximum fine, with a default of four months in jail, after Abdullah Mustakim, 33, pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to the pupil in a classroom at a school here at about 2.30 pm on Oct 23, 2024. The kick caused an injury to the pupil’s gums.

items.title: Anwar courts Chinese industry leaders with eye on investments in chips, AI and robotics
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — A roundtable discussion with industry leaders from 21 leading Chinese companies here focused on various high-impact sectors, including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics, as Malaysia explores high-value strategic investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The discussion also touched on the potential of electric vehicles (EVs), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology, healthcare, specialty chemicals and advanced manufacturing. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook also participated in the discussion.

items.title: Rosmah’s RM67.5m jewellery bill: No pause button, Court of Appeal rules
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has lost her latest bid to fully halt a RM67.5 million payment owed to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL over dozens of missing jewellery pieces. The Court of Appeal has dismissed her appeal against a High Court order for a conditional stay, meaning the sum must still be deposited into a stakeholder account within a month of the August 12 judgement, The Edge reported today. The dispute traces back to a June High Court ruling by Judicial Commissioner Datuk Quay Chew Soon, which held Rosmah liable for 43 pieces of jewellery that went missing after a 2018 police raid.

items.title: Zero motions, zero Bills: Dewan Rakyat Speaker still waiting on no-confidence bid, PM term-limit, and AG-PP split
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 23 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said he has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting. Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure. Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.

items.title: Three-day remand for two men as Sarawak police probe convenience store fire cases
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Two men aged 40 and 23 were remanded for three days by the Magistrates’ Court here today to assist investigations into a case of mischief by fire involving a convenience store along Jalan Green here. The court ordered both suspects to be remanded for three days from Sept 23 to Sept 26 to assist investigations under Section 436 of the Penal Code. Three suspects have been arrested and remanded to assist investigations into both incidents.

items.title: Haze eases in Lubok Antu, but Kanowit air remains ‘very unhealthy’ at midday
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Lubok Antu moved out of the very unhealthy category by noon today after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropped from 205 at 8am to 195. Most monitoring stations across Sarawak also remained in the unhealthy category at noon, with readings ranging from 105 to 195. Under the API classification, readings of 0–50 are considered good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy and 201–300 very unhealthy.

items.title: Teen accused in Bandar Utama school killing diagnosed with early-onset schizophrenia and viewed others as ‘non-player characters’
items.summary: In her full grounds of judgment, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said this was disclosed in a psychiatric report prepared by Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, the director and senior consultant forensic psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta. In disclosing his findings, Dr Ian highlighted the existence of a “ Death Note ” journal on the accused’s mobile phone, in which he repeatedly referred to the deceased while chronicling the disturbing and psychotic thoughts in his mind. Psychiatric report findings The psychiatric report also noted a strong family history of mental illness, including an institutionalised aunt, a mentally disordered paternal grand-uncle and two affected sons, as well as a family member treated for depression.

items.title: ‘Your country is proud of you’, Anwar tells 22 Malaysians competing at WorldSkills Shanghai
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hailed Malaysia’s 22 young competitors at the 48th WorldSkills Competition here as the country’s pride, stressing that skilled workers are indispensable to a modern, technology-driven economy. Touching on youth’s role in the economy, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said young skilled workers play a crucial role in keeping modern economies running, even as machinery and software become increasingly sophisticated. Anwar said young people would be drawn to technical and skilled professions if they could see clear prospects for career advancement and better livelihoods.

items.title: Overseas markets key to growing Malaysia’s oil and gas services sector in next three years, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The government expects the oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) sector to increase its output and revenue in the next two to three years through expansion into overseas markets, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. Speaking to reporters today, he said greater international market participation would strengthen the sector’s revenue streams while improving the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies against economic and industry shocks. Akmal Nasrullah said international diversification was important to strengthen the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies and reduce their reliance on the domestic market.

items.title: New Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route on the cards as China Eastern eyes more Sabah flights
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — China Eastern Airlines plans to increase its Shanghai-Kota Kinabalu services to double or even triple daily flights, while exploring a direct Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route. Also present were Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry Permanent Secretary Datuk Josie Lai and representatives from the Sabah Tourism Board. — Daily Express Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin (centre) receives a memento from China Eastern Airlines (Sales & Marketing) Senior Vice President Yang Chun Fei (left).

items.title: Health Ministry van carrying trainee nurses ends up on its side in Ipoh crash, nine injured
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Nine people were injured when a Health Ministry van overturned and landed on its driver’s side in an accident along Jalan Sultan Iskandar near Little India in Ipoh this morning. The van was carrying trainee nurses from the Health Ministry’s Sultan Azlan Shah Training Institute in Tanjung Rambutan, according to a report by the New Straits Times . Najib said police were investigating the cause of the accident.

items.title: Perhilitan sets tiger trap in Sungai Siput village after fatal attack on Orang Asli man
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 23 — Personnel from the People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela) assisted the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) in setting up a tiger trap in Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor, following a tiger attack that claimed the life of an Orang Asli resident last Monday. According to a Facebook post by Rela Sungai Siput (North) district office, several members were deployed to assist Perhilitan, help ensure the safety of local residents and address the threat posed by the animal. The media reported yesterday that an Orang Asli man, Zamberi Angah, 42, died after a suspected tiger attack while foraging for rattan in the Korbu Forest Reserve near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor, Sungai Siput.

items.title: Meeting between Negeri Sembilan MB, exco and Tunku Nadzaruddin cancelled over safety concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — A scheduled meeting between Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, state executive councillors and Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was cancelled this morning due to safety considerations. The source said Ismail instead had breakfast with exco members and several government assemblymen earlier today. “The Menteri Besar only had breakfast with the exco and several government assemblymen,” the source said.

items.title: Malaysia ready to lead Asean’s green jobs push, says Anwar
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Malaysia underscored its regional leadership in skills development and green workforce readiness at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Conference, reaffirming its long-standing commitment to elevating technical and vocational excellence. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim highlighted the country’s newly entrusted role to lead the regional green jobs agenda following the Asean Plus Three Labour Ministers Meeting in Bangkok. Malaysia has sent 22 young competitors across 21 skill areas.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia needs skilled workers to power its next economic leap
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Malaysia is positioning Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) at the centre of its industrial policy, making it a key instrument of economic transformation to build a highly skilled and well-paid workforce. He said the ‘TVET 2.0’ reform phase aims to promote closer collaboration between industry players and training institutions while accelerating exposure to emerging fields such as semiconductors, AI and renewable energy. Coordination of the national agenda is managed by the National TVET Council across around 1,400 institutions, involving 12 ministries, state governments and private providers, under the National TVET Policy 2030, he said.
